label: Models of complex systems should first be judged by comparing overall pictures
claim: For systems with complex behavior, a model cannot be adequately assessed by matching a few extracted numbers; the best first test is a visual comparison of the model's overall behavior with that of the real system.
quote: by far the best first step in assessing a model is not to look at numbers or other details, but rather just to use one's eyes, and to compare overall pictures of a system with pictures from the model.
scope: scientific modelling of systems with complex behavior
candidate_data: none known

label: Snowflake shapes arise from growth inhibition captured by a hexagonal cellular automaton
claim: The main features of snowflake shapes are reproduced by a hexagonal cellular automaton in which a cell becomes ice only if exactly one neighbor is ice, which represents the inhibition of nearby growth by released latent heat.
quote: One can capture this basic effect by having a cellular automaton with rules in which cells become black if they have exactly one black neighbor, but stay white whenever they have more than one black neighbor.
scope: growth of snowflakes (ice crystals from water vapor)
measurable_quantities: morphology of snowflakes compared with cellular automaton patterns at various steps
branching and faceting statistics of snow crystals
candidate_data: Published snowflake photograph collections (e.g. W. A. Bentley's and K. Libbrecht's) and laboratory snow-crystal growth studies.

label: Growing snowflakes should alternate between tree-like and faceted shapes
claim: During the growth of an individual snowflake its shape should alternate between tree-like and faceted forms, as new branches grow and then collide with one another.
quote: one expects that during the growth of a particular snowflake there should be alternation between tree-like and faceted shapes, as new branches grow but then collide with each other.
scope: time course of individual snowflake growth
measurable_quantities: time-lapse sequence of snow crystal shape during growth
presence of facet-enclosed regions alternating with dendritic arms
candidate_data: Laboratory time-lapse imaging of growing snow crystals and published snowflake photograph collections showing internal growth rings.

label: Randomness in crystal shapes is often intrinsically generated by simple growth rules
claim: Apparent randomness in the shapes of crystalline materials often arises intrinsically from simple deterministic growth rules, rather than from randomness in the seed or the growth environment.
quote: And contrary to what has always been assumed, I suspect that this is actually how the apparent randomness that one sometimes sees in shapes formed by crystalline materials often comes about.
scope: growth shapes of crystals
measurable_quantities: shape irregularity of crystals grown under controlled, uniform conditions from controlled seeds
reproducibility of crystal shapes across repeated growth runs
candidate_data: Controlled crystal-growth experiments in the materials-science literature; no specific public dataset known.

label: Randomness of fracture surfaces comes from a material-independent intrinsic mechanism
claim: The roughness and randomness of fracture paths does not come from random irregularities in a material but from a general mechanism in which deterministic interactions of element displacements around a moving crack intrinsically generate randomness, as in a simple cellular automaton model.
quote: I nevertheless suspect that even when much more realistic models for specific materials are used, the fundamental mechanisms responsible for randomness will still be very much the same as in the extremely simple model shown here.
scope: fracture of solids, from single crystals to geological faults
measurable_quantities: roughness statistics of fracture surfaces in single crystals versus polycrystalline materials
scaling of fracture roughness across length scales
candidate_data: Published fractography and fracture-surface roughness measurements (e.g. silicon single-crystal fracture studies and geological fault-surface profiles).

label: Conservation plus microscopic randomness yields universal fluid behavior
claim: Any system of particles that conserves quantities such as particle number and momentum and has sufficient microscopic randomness will show the same large-scale fluid behavior, so a discrete cellular automaton particle model can reproduce the flow of real fluids.
quote: so long as certain physical quantities such as particle number and momentum are conserved, then whenever there is sufficient microscopic randomness, it is almost inevitable that the same overall fluid behavior will be obtained.
scope: fluids and discrete lattice-gas models of fluids
measurable_quantities: large-scale velocity fields from lattice-gas simulations versus experiments at matched Reynolds number
eddy formation and shedding thresholds
candidate_data: Lattice-gas and lattice-Boltzmann simulation codes and published experimental measurements of flow past cylinders (vortex shedding).

label: Large-scale fluid flow shows little sensitive dependence on initial conditions
claim: In almost all cases, large-scale fluid behavior does not depend discernibly on the detailed initial conditions; small perturbations are damped out by viscosity, so sensitive dependence (chaos) is the exception rather than the rule.
quote: when it comes to large-scale fluid behavior, it seems to be true that in almost all cases there is no discernible difference between what happens with different detailed initial conditions.
scope: large-scale behavior of real and model fluid flows, including turbulence
measurable_quantities: divergence of large-scale flow fields from slightly perturbed initial conditions
ensemble spread of repeated turbulence experiments
candidate_data: Johns Hopkins Turbulence Database and direct numerical simulation codes, plus repeated-run laboratory flow experiments.

label: Turbulent randomness is intrinsically generated at the level of large-scale fluid motion
claim: The randomness seen in turbulent fluids is mostly neither inserted from outside nor inherited from molecular randomness, but is intrinsically generated by the dynamics of the large-scale fluid motion itself.
quote: Instead, what seems to be happening is that intrinsic randomness generation occurs directly at the level of large-scale fluid motion.
scope: turbulent fluid flow
measurable_quantities: randomness of large-scale flow under highly controlled, simple initial and boundary conditions
correlation between molecular-scale perturbations and large-scale flow
candidate_data: Johns Hopkins Turbulence Database and published controlled turbulence experiments.

label: Random-looking yet repeatable fluid flows should be producible
claim: Because turbulent randomness is generated intrinsically by large-scale motion, carefully prepared experiments should produce fluid flows that look random yet are essentially the same on every repeated run.
quote: with sufficiently careful preparation it should be possible to produce patterns of flow that seem quite random but that are nevertheless effectively repeatable—so that they look essentially the same on every successive run of an experiment.
scope: laboratory fluid flows at turbulent or near-turbulent conditions
measurable_quantities: run-to-run correlation of complex flow patterns under identical preparation
complexity or entropy of the flow pattern
candidate_data: Published vortex-interaction experiments; new repeated-run laboratory flow visualization would be needed.

label: Most biological complexity comes from randomly chosen programs, not natural selection
claim: Most of the complexity seen in biological organisms originates from the abstract fact that many randomly chosen programs produce complex behavior, rather than from adaptation or careful optimization by natural selection.
quote: the vast majority of the complexity we see in biological systems actually has its origin in the purely abstract fact that among randomly chosen programs many give rise to complex behavior.
scope: complex forms and patterns in biological organisms
measurable_quantities: fitness effects of complex versus simple pattern details
frequency of complex behavior among random genetic or developmental variants
candidate_data: none known

label: Evolution cannot have found optimal solutions to complex fitness constraints
claim: Since iterative random search converges only for simple constraints, the roughly trillion generations of life on Earth are insufficient to find optimal solutions to complex constraints, so most features of organisms are merely good-enough solutions rather than optima.
quote: it is still completely implausible that the trillion or so generations of organisms since the beginning of life on Earth would be sufficient to allow optimal solutions to be found to constraints of any significant complexity.
scope: biological evolution as an iterative random search
measurable_quantities: convergence time of mutation-selection search on fitness landscapes of varying complexity
distance of observed traits from engineering optima
candidate_data: Computational evolution and fitness-landscape simulations; published experimental evolution studies.

label: Complexity of individual organism parts has been roughly constant for eons
claim: The complexity of individual parts of organisms, such as textures and other morphological features, was already present in early fossils and has not changed much in at least several hundred million years.
quote: there is every indication that the level of complexity of individual parts of organisms has not changed much in at least several hundred million years.
scope: fossil record of morphological complexity
measurable_quantities: quantitative complexity measures of fossil textures and ornamentation over geological time
candidate_data: Paleobiology Database and published morphological-complexity time series from the fossil record.

label: Features that change fastest between species are the most complex
claim: Among related species, the features that differ most rapidly (such as pigmentation and texture patterns) are the ones that show the most obvious complexity, while features under natural selection stay nearly constant.
quote: it is almost always those features which change most rapidly between species that show the most obvious signs of complexity.
scope: variation of traits among closely related species
measurable_quantities: rate of interspecific change of traits
complexity measure of each trait
candidate_data: Comparative phylogenetic trait datasets and image collections of pigmentation in fishes, butterflies and molluscs.

label: Genetic programs for complex pigment patterns are short
claim: The genetic programs that generate patterns such as those on mollusc shells are short, as indicated by the large variety of patterns within species, and molecular biology should be able to isolate them and confirm their brevity.
quote: Modern molecular biology should soon be able to isolate the specific programs responsible, say, for the patterns on mollusc shells, and see explicitly how long they are. But there are already indications that these programs are quite short.
scope: genetic control of pigmentation patterns, especially on mollusc shells
measurable_quantities: number of genes and regulatory elements controlling shell pigmentation
intraspecific pattern variability
candidate_data: Mollusc genome assemblies and shell-pigmentation gene-expression studies in NCBI GenBank and the published literature.

label: Natural selection works meaningfully only on simple behavior
claim: The power of natural selection is limited: it can systematically optimize only systems or parts of systems whose behavior is simple, and achieves very little when behavior is complex.
quote: what I suspect is that in the end natural selection can only operate in a meaningful way on systems or parts of systems whose behavior is in some sense quite simple.
scope: natural selection acting on biological traits
measurable_quantities: response to selection of simple versus complex traits
success of iterative random search on simple versus complex target behaviors
candidate_data: Artificial-selection and experimental-evolution datasets; evolutionary computation benchmarks.

label: Natural selection makes organisms simpler and more engineering-like
claim: Rather than generating complexity, the main effect of natural selection is to make biological systems avoid complexity, favoring simple, somewhat independent components with smoothly adjustable properties, as in engineered systems.
quote: my strong suspicion is that in fact the main effect of natural selection is almost exactly the opposite: it tends to make biological systems avoid complexity, and be more like systems in engineering.
scope: biological organisms under natural selection
measurable_quantities: modularity and smoothness of variation in selected traits
complexity of traits under strong versus weak selection
candidate_data: Quantitative-genetics datasets from plant and animal breeding; comparative morphology databases.

label: Convergent structures recur because they are common among programs, not optimal
claim: When similar complex structures arise independently in very different organisms, this is because those structures are common outputs of programs of certain kinds, not because they are optimal.
quote: the reason certain structures appear repeatedly is just that they are somehow common among programs of certain kinds
scope: convergent evolution
measurable_quantities: frequency of convergent structures among outputs of random developmental programs
optimality of convergent structures
candidate_data: none known

label: Natural selection does not inherently drive organisms toward more elaborate structure
claim: Natural selection does not inevitably produce progressively more elaborate organisms; increases in complexity in the fossil record come from random mutations that add features without fatal flaws, while selection's systematic effect is to simplify.
quote: It is certainly not the case—as is often assumed—that natural selection somehow inevitably leads to organisms with progressively more elaborate structures and progressively larger numbers of parts.
scope: long-term trends in organismal complexity
measurable_quantities: trends in number of parts or cell types across lineages over time
frequency of simplification versus elaboration events
candidate_data: Paleobiology Database and published studies of trends in organismal complexity (e.g. cell-type counts across lineages).

label: Plant branching patterns come from simple substitution-system growth rules
claim: The overall branching patterns of plants, from algae to ferns to trees and flowering plants, are produced by simple growth rules in which each stem tip repeatedly splits into smaller copies of itself at fixed relative lengths and angles.
quote: And no doubt it is from such simple rules of growth that most such overall branching patterns come.
scope: overall branching architecture of plants
measurable_quantities: branch length ratios and branching angles
fit of substitution-system models to measured plant architectures
candidate_data: Plant architecture measurements and L-system modelling literature; 3D plant scan datasets.

label: Leaf shapes arise from the same simple branching process as whole plants
claim: The shapes of leaves, from smooth to prickly to irregular, are produced by the same simple branching growth process that governs overall plant forms, and small changes in its parameters can change leaf shape greatly.
quote: I strongly suspect that in fact the very same simple process of branching is ultimately responsible both for the overall forms of plants, and for the shapes of their leaves.
scope: leaf shape development in plants
measurable_quantities: leaf outline shapes versus outlines of substitution-system patterns
relation of early vein patterns to final leaf outlines
candidate_data: Leaf image collections and herbarium digitizations (e.g. iDigBio, Leafsnap dataset) and leaf developmental studies.

label: The 137.5° phyllotaxis angle results from a simple inhibition growth process
claim: The near-universal 137.5° (golden-ratio) angle between successive plant organs is not an optimization found by natural selection but the inevitable result of a simple process where each new element forms where a chemical concentration is highest and depletes it nearby.
quote: And instead what I strongly suspect is that the patterns are just inevitable consequences of a rather simple process of growth not unlike one that was already discussed, at least in general terms, nearly a century ago.
scope: phyllotaxis and spiral arrangements of plant organs
measurable_quantities: divergence angles between successive organs
convergence of inhibition-model simulations to 137.5° across damping values
hormone concentration patterns at the shoot apex
candidate_data: Published phyllotaxis divergence-angle measurements and auxin-distribution imaging studies of shoot apical meristems.

label: Simple growth-rate models generate essentially all mollusc shell shapes
claim: Mollusc shell shapes result from secreting material at different rates around the shell opening, and essentially every form produced by a simple growth model with a few parameters is found in some real mollusc.
quote: The remarkable fact illustrated on the next page is that essentially all of them are found in some kind of mollusc or another.
scope: coiled shell shapes of molluscs
measurable_quantities: shell growth parameters (expansion rate, translation, aperture shape) of real species
occupancy of the model parameter space by real species
candidate_data: Shell morphometric datasets and museum shell collections; published theoretical-morphospace studies of coiled shells.

label: Animal embryos develop hierarchically because of a fixed length scale
claim: Because regions of tissue a few tenths of a millimeter across subdivide into regions using different sections of the genetic program (controlled by chemical gradients and homeobox genes), embryos necessarily develop hierarchically, e.g. a leg region before a foot region.
quote: The existence of a fixed length scale at which such processes occur then almost inevitably implies that an embryo must develop in a somewhat hierarchical fashion.
scope: embryonic development of animals
measurable_quantities: size of tissue regions at the time of subdivision
morphogen gradient length scales
order of appearance of nested anatomical regions
candidate_data: Developmental biology atlases and morphogen-gradient measurements in the literature (e.g. Drosophila and vertebrate limb studies).

label: Shape differences between related animals come from differing growth rates
claim: Differences in shape among related animals are largely due to different patterns of relative growth rates of their parts, so their shapes are related by simple smooth geometric transformations.
quote: differences between the shapes and forms of animals may often be due in large part merely to different patterns in the rates of growth for their different parts.
scope: body shapes of animals within a family or order
measurable_quantities: geometric-morphometric landmark transformations between species
allometric growth coefficients
candidate_data: Geometric morphometrics landmark datasets (e.g. MorphoSource specimen scans) and published allometry studies.

label: Diversity of plant and animal forms comes from different simple rules
claim: Most of the diversity and complexity in the forms of plants and animals arises because slightly different, essentially randomly picked simple growth rules lead to very different and often complex behavior.
quote: it is this basic phenomenon that I suspect is responsible for most of the diversity and complexity that we see in the forms of plants and animals.
scope: forms of plants and animals
measurable_quantities: sensitivity of developmental outcomes to small rule changes
match between simple-rule model outputs and observed morphological diversity
candidate_data: none known

label: Mollusc shell pigment patterns are generated like one-dimensional cellular automata
claim: Pigmentation patterns on mollusc shells are produced line by line by pigment-secreting elements whose new states depend on neighbors' previous states, so the range of shell patterns closely matches the patterns of the simplest symmetric one-dimensional cellular automata.
quote: comparing the patterns in these pictures with patterns on actual mollusc shells, one notices the remarkable fact that the range of patterns that occur in the two cases is extremely similar.
scope: pigmentation patterns on mollusc shells
measurable_quantities: classification of shell patterns into cellular automaton behavior classes
statistical comparison of shell pattern features with cellular automaton outputs
candidate_data: Published shell-pattern image collections and museum mollusc collections.

label: Mollusc shell pattern rules are effectively random, not optimized
claim: The rules generating mollusc shell patterns are effectively chosen at random from the simplest possibilities rather than optimized against predators or for mates, as shown by many species whose patterns are hidden by opaque skin throughout life.
quote: these patterns are instead generated by rules that are in effect chosen at random from among a collection of the simplest possibilities.
scope: evolution of mollusc shell pigmentation
measurable_quantities: prevalence of complex patterns in species whose shells are covered in life
phylogenetic signal and selective correlates of shell patterns
candidate_data: Museum mollusc collections with periostracum and habitat records; comparative phylogenetic studies of shell coloration.

label: Animal coat patterns arise from local activation and longer-range inhibition rules
claim: The few recurring kinds of animal pigmentation patterns (spots, labyrinths, stripes) are produced by a simple rule in which each element tends to match the average color of nearby elements and oppose that of elements further away, as in a two-dimensional cellular automaton.
quote: The idea is that when a pattern forms, the color of each element will tend to be the same as the average color of nearby elements, and opposite to the average color of elements further away.
scope: pigmentation patterns on animal skins and coats
measurable_quantities: spatial statistics of real coat patterns versus model outputs
short-range activation and long-range inhibition between pigment cells
candidate_data: Animal coat-pattern image collections and published zebrafish pigment-cell interaction experiments.

label: Short-timescale market randomness comes from internal market dynamics
claim: Much of the apparent randomness in financial prices, especially on timescales of minutes or seconds, is generated by the internal dynamics of trading entities interacting with one another, not by external news or changes in the value of the asset.
quote: particularly on short timescales much of the randomness that one sees is purely a consequence of internal dynamics in the market, and has little if anything to do with the nature or value of what is being traded.
scope: price fluctuations in financial markets
measurable_quantities: intraday price volatility versus news arrival
volatility during purely speculative trading
autocorrelation and entropy of high-frequency returns
candidate_data: CRSP or other market tick data (e.g. NYSE TAQ) combined with timestamped news feeds.

label: Simple cellular automaton markets generate random-looking price series
claim: In a market modelled as a one-dimensional cellular automaton of buy/sell agents reacting to neighbors, any rule that lets information eventually propagate to all agents makes the running buy-minus-sell total show significant randomness.
quote: as soon as the underlying rule for the cellular automaton is such that information will eventually propagate from one entity to all others—in effect a minimal version of an efficient market hypothesis—it is essentially inevitable that running totals of numbers of cells will exhibit significant randomness.
scope: one-dimensional cellular automaton models of markets
measurable_quantities: randomness tests on running totals of cell colors for all rules with full information propagation
candidate_data: Direct enumeration and simulation of elementary cellular automata with standard software.
